span.label: the incompatibility holds except in highly constrained special cases

span.label: The computational tractability of finding a minimum-loss fair assignment (or even deciding whether a non-trivial one exists) is left open.
span.note: what this limits: any algorithmic use of the fairness conditions: IT IS AN OPEN QUESTION WHETHER THERE IS A POLYNOMIAL-TIME ALGORITHM TO FIND A FAIR ASSIGNMENT OF MINIMUM LOSS, OR EVEN TO DETERMINE WHETHER A NON-TRIVIAL FAIR SOLUTION EXISTS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The NP-completeness result covers only the integral case, not the general model where a feature vector may be split across bins.
span.note: what this limits: the NP-completeness result only: IT APPLIES ONLY TO THE CASE IN WHICH EVERYONE WITH A GIVEN FEATURE VECTOR MUST BE ASSIGNED TO THE SAME BIN
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper deliberately does not analyse which fairness definitions are violated in real applications or datasets.
span.note: what this limits: any applied reading of the impossibility result: NOR IS OUR INTENTION TO ANALYZE WHICH DEFINITIONS OF FAIRNESS ARE VIOLATED IN PARTICULAR APPLICATIONS OR DATASETS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The exposition is restricted to two groups.
span.note: what this limits: the two-group presentation: WE FOCUS ON THE CASE OF TWO GROUPS FOR SIMPLICITY OF EXPOSITION, with extension described as straightforward
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The model assumes the true positive-class rate for each feature vector is known to the procedure; the unknown case is not analysed.
span.note: what this limits: the known-p-sigma assumption, and the direction it cuts: THE CASE IN WHICH THE VALUE OF p-sigma IS UNKNOWN IS AN IMPORTANT VERSION OF THE PROBLEM AS WELL; HOWEVER, SINCE OUR MAIN RESULTS ESTABLISH STRONG LIMITATIONS ON WHAT IS ACHIEVABLE, THESE LIMI[tations carry over]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Withholding the group attribute from the procedure does not stop it exhibiting bias between groups, and the paper says so in a parenthesis as it defines the model.
span.note: what this limits: a claim that a procedure is unbiased because it never sees group membership: this model's rule has access only to the feature vector, and the authors state that this does not mean the rule is incapable of exhibiting bias between the two groups
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The modelling assumption that group membership adds nothing beyond the feature vector is defended by a construction in which the feature vector conveys group perfectly.
span.note: what this limits: the generality claimed for this model: the assumption that group adds no information beyond the feature vector is justified by allowing instances where people of different groups never share a feature vector, so that the feature vector implicitly conveys the group
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A fourth and legally mandated notion of fairness is set aside as often neither feasible nor desirable, so the impossibility result does not speak to it.
span.note: what this limits: this theorem as covering fairness generally: statistical parity is excluded from the three conditions, on the stated ground that classification and risk assessment are broader activities where it is often neither feasible nor desirable
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: calibration (well-calibrated risk score)
span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED. The published string was not verbatim in EITHER copy of the paper. A quote field promises the author's words; this held `the average probability of recidivism are equally well calibrated`. The paper says `ITS ESTIMATES OF the probability of recidivism`. `The average probability` is this paper's term for a DIFFERENT criterion - the global requirement it calls statistical parity, and explicitly distinguishes from calibration. The rewrite imported the name of the thing being contrasted with.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
